Entities / Places / Dath Mar

Dath-Mar

A hard place kept for hard hours.

The smallest of the five Sunken Crown islands. Its name preserves the local tabaxi sense of strengthened stone — a place of endurance rather than comfort. A few individuals live there year-round by choice. Most use it only when they need to.

Keth-Naar hunters retreat here when a storm splits boats from home, when someone needs distance from the central settlement, or when a decision is too heavy to bring to the elders without sitting with it first. The island’s value is not what it offers — it can hold a person above the water when the rest of the Blue Hole turns against them.

Geography

A hard, exposed rock with leeward approaches, a sheltered cut, black stone, higher cracks, and tide-dependent access. Not comfortable. Not meant to be. The current reversals around the Blue Hole have made the approach less predictable — skiffs strand on the wrong side of the rock more often than they used to.

The Cairns

Cairns mark the leeward approaches and the sheltered cut. They are maintained by whoever last used them. Leaving one worse than you found it is a serious breach — the next arrival may not have the luxury of doing without it.

People & Power

Dath-Mar is held by Keth-Naar custom rather than occupation. The rule is maintenance: leave worse than you found, and the next arrival pays for it.

Trade & Resources

No trade. Its resource is survival space: a place to wait out weather, separation, or a decision that cannot yet be brought home.

Fauna

Giant lizards sun against the black stone after storms. Giant bats use the higher cracks when weather grounds them. Giant crabs work the tidal zone at the island’s base — the cairn approaches pass through crab territory at low water. Keth-Naar hunters harvest selectively, managing the count without eliminating the population.

Hazards

Exposure, current reversals, tide windows, lizards, bats, crabs, and failing predictability around the Blue Hole.

Current Hooks

  • Current reversals have made skiffs strand on the wrong side of the rock more often — the approach has become unreliable.
  • If the refuge stops functioning, Keth-Naar loses its safest fallback during storms.
